notes: Roon connects again — a regression I introduced in 0.2.9. Pairing is the one flow that makes you leave the app: you open Roon, go to Settings > Extensions and click Enable, and Roon's answer comes back over the socket this app is holding. Up to 0.2.8 the service was in the foreground all the time, so the process survived that trip; from 0.2.9 it was only foreground during a migration, so Android froze it the moment you switched to Roon and the pairing never completed. It now holds the process while Roon is discovering, connecting or waiting for your approval — minutes at most, so it cannot run into the six-hour limit that caused the 0.2.5 crash. And the second half of why that was unrecoverable: "Find my Roon Core" did literally nothing, silently, once a first attempt had been interrupted — for the rest of the app's life. Pressing it now restarts a dead attempt, while still leaving a live one alone so a double tap cannot pull the socket out from under an approval. RoonCore also has real tests on the Android side for the first time; it had none, which is why a bug in both halves went unnoticed. The protection is bounded to five minutes from the button press: with no Core on the network Roon discovery retries for ever, and keying it off the stage alone held the foreground service open indefinitely — which is the same budget whose exhaustion caused the 0.2.5 crash. Caught on an emulator.
